newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India buys three diesel cargoes in April tender.
newsitem.headline: India buys three diesel cargoes in April tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has bought three cargoes of diesel in its second tender for April delivery, traders said on Monday.

European major British Petroleum was awarded one 1.0 percent sulphur cargo at U.S.$20.48 per tonne above the high of Mediterranean quotes, cost and freight (CNF) Kandla on the Indian west coast. Dutch trader Vitol was awarded a 1.0 percent sulphur cargo at $27.05 per tonne above the mean of Mediterranean quotes and a 0.5 percent sulphur cargo at $29.08 per tonne above the mean of Mediterranean quotes, CNF Kandla.
Each cargo is 40,000 to 45,000 tonnes. India had originally sought six cargoes in this tender. In its first tender for April delivery, India bought 570,000 tonnes of diesel in 15 cargoes.
